The letter does not disclose which of these applies.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The denial letter identifies the payer only as 'Medicaid, state of Georgia' without naming the specific administering entity. Georgia Medicaid is delivered either through fee-for-service (administered by the GA Dept. of Community Health) or through one of several private Care Management Organizations (CMOs) under the 'Georgia Families' managed-care program (Amerigroup/Wellpoint, CareSource, Peach State Health Plan/Centene, or Humana Healthy Horizons). Each of these entities maintains its own separate clinical/medical-necessity policy for total hip arthroplasty (CPT 27130), typically built on a third-party criteria set (e.g., InterQual or MCG) plus plan-specific medical policy bulletins; none of these are unified into one public 'Georgia Medicaid' policy for this procedure. The letter itself does not name the specific CMO or confirm FFS status, which is necessary to identify the correct governing document, since each CMO applies its own (often licensed, not fully public) clinical criteria. I did find, for reference only, a CMS document titled '0184-Total Hip Arthroplasty: Medical Necessity and Documentation Requirements' covering CPT 27130/27132/27134/27137/27138, but this is a Medicare program-integrity/compliance resource tied to Medicare Administrative Contractors (FCSO, NGS, Novitas, Palmetto, Noridian, WPS, CGS) — it is NOT a Georgia Medicaid document and should not be cited as the basis for this Medicaid denial. I also found that Georgia Medicaid CMOs (e.g., Peach State Health Plan, CareSource) publish member appeal timelines of 60 calendar days from the adverse benefit determination notice — shorter than the 180 days stated in this letter — so the patient should treat 180 days with caution and confirm the true deadline directly with whichever plan issued this denial, and should not delay filing. Given the reason cited ('documentation incomplete') rather than a specific clinical-criteria failure, the most actionable immediate step is for the provider to resubmit with complete clinical documentation (imaging, conservative treatment history, functional/pain assessments) rather than to rebut clinical criteria the payer has not yet clearly cited.
